newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index edges up in heavier activity.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index edges up in heavier activity.

text.p: Leading Slovak shares closed mixed in heavier activity on the Bratislava Stock Exchange on Tuesday, with gains to crude oil refiner Slovnaft inching the SAX index 0.04 points up to 220.55.
Slovnaft, the most-capitalised issue on the 12-share index, led the bourse with 16,030 shares traded, closing up 50 crowns, or 5.26 percent, at its 1,000 crown nominal value.
"Slovnaft's close is appropriate to the volume traded, proving perhaps some decent interest, but without any competition to drive it higher," said Patrik Granec of Slovenska Sporitelna.
Added Vladimir Kuklis, an analyst with CSOB Bank in Bratislava: "I see Slovnaft headed rather down."
Brokers said the replacement of three key government ministers did not appear to have any immediate effect on the market.

The country's largest credit bank, VUB, closed down 150 crowns at 2,100, as other blue chips, gas storage firm Nafta and plastics producer Plastika, took a breather. VSZ steel closed down 20 crowns, or 2.58 percent, at 645 crowns.
"The market is weakening price-wise, being overheated at its peak (shares) and its recent uptrend should reverse," Kuklis added.
Overall volume rose to 240,279 shares traded from 100,369 shares on Monday, while turnover increased to 177.32 million crowns from 51.45 million.
